results.title: Plain delete latency baseline (upstream #4697)
results.desc: DeleteSandbox on healthy sandbox; measure full-removal time
results.detail: delete grpc=0; fully gone in 2.8s (baseline for #4697 opt-in timeout)
results.prose: Upstream #4697 added an opt-in delete timeout to the Python client because deletes can hang on slow workloads. I measured the healthy-workload baseline on the gRPC path: a plain sleep-300 sandbox, deleted via DeleteSandbox, fully disappeared from the gateway in 2.8s. That's the number a client-side timeout has to accommodate before it's safe to abandon a delete — anything tighter than ~30s risks declaring failure while the supervisor is still doing honest, bounded work (we saw 33s on a TERM-ignoring workload in the 02:10Z cycle).
results.steps: CreateSandbox sleep 300; wait Ready; DeleteSandbox; poll GetSandbox until grpc=5; measure elapsed.
